column11: the layer is an age extension, so this share converts the book's adult pool into the adolescent population the study actually adds. Qulipta is approved for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults and only adults (DailyMed set id 8c8ab8f4-32bd-497a-befa-70c8a51d8d52, revised 2025-09-30), and of the two studies on this unit NCT06241313 enrols adults (in label, already inside the $1,036mm) while NCT06810505 enrols chronic migraine at ages 12 to 17 (ClinicalTrials.gov, read 2026-10-27, 420 participants, primary completion 2031-03). Two sourced numbers give that population: the US adolescent (12-17) chronic migraine prevalence of 0.79% excluding medication overuse from Lipton RB, Manack A, Ricci JA, Chee E, Turkel CC, Winner P, 'Prevalence and burden of chronic migraine in adolescents: results of the chronic daily headache in adolescents study (C-dAS)', Headache 2011;51(5):693-706, PMID 21521206, doi 10.1111/j.1526-4610.2011.01885.x, a US Census-balanced household sample with a 30-day diary; and 26,038,160 US residents aged 12 to 17 at 1 July 2024 (Census nc-est2024-agesex-res, summed over single years of age 12 to 17). 0.0079 x 26,038,160 = 205,701 patients, and 205,701 / 31,236,457 = 0.0065853

column11: a judgement. The competitive case: nothing in the CGRP class is labelled for migraine prevention in anyone under 18, so a positive NCT06810505 would make atogepant the first, against topiramate and propranolol as the incumbent oral preventives. Against that, the pool is adolescents with chronic migraine, the C-dAS paper reports that about 60% of them had not seen a healthcare provider in the previous year and fewer than one in five were taking any preventive, so diagnosis rather than competition is the binding constraint
